tool.help:
Multiple sequence alignment analysis ------------------------------------ The **current Galaxy Tool** is the implementation of the Bio2Byte tools for the analysis of **multiple sequence alignments**. It receives an existing alignment of protein sequences and returns the biophysical predictions of every sequence mapped onto the alignment, together with the distribution of each predicted feature along the alignment.
Use the companion tool *b2bTools: Biophysical predictors for single sequences* when your sequences are not aligned.
Input alignment ''''''''''''''' The input must be an existing alignment in **FASTA**, **CLUSTAL** or **Stockholm** format. All the sequences must share the same aligned length; the tool fails if they do not, because the predicted values could not be compared position by position.
Gap positions (``-``) carry no predicted value: they appear in the tabular output with an empty cell and in the JSON output as ``null``.
Each sequence must have at least 5 residues, gaps excluded.
@HELP_PREDICTORS@
Expected results '''''''''''''''' From a single alignment of N sequences and L alignment columns, the process will produce:
- **Predictions by aligned residue**: one tabular file with N x L rows. The first three columns are ``sequence_id``, ``residue_index`` (the zero-based alignment position) and ``residue``; the remaining columns are the predicted features of the selected predictors. - **Distribution of predictions along the alignment**: one tabular file summarising, for every alignment position and predicted feature, how the values are distributed across the sequences. - **Predictions in JSON format**: the aligned sequences and the predicted values of each sequence. - **N tabular results**: the same table as above, split into one file per sequence. - **Distribution plots** (in case the user checked the ``plot`` parameter): one chart per predicted feature showing the median, the interquartile range and the outlier boundaries along the alignment, named after the feature, for instance ``backbone.png``. - **Aligned value plots** (in case the user checked the ``plot_aligned`` parameter): one chart per predicted feature drawing one line per sequence against the alignment position, so the sequences can be compared position by position. They are named after the feature with an ``aligned_`` prefix, for instance ``aligned_backbone.png``. Gap positions carry no value, so the line of a sequence is interrupted wherever it has a gap.
Checking **Highlight regions of interest** shades the biophysical regions on the background of both kinds of chart, exactly as the single sequence tool does. Only ``backbone``, ``earlyFolding`` and ``disoMine`` have defined regions; the charts of the other features are left unshaded.
Predictions by aligned residue ..............................
::
sequence_id residue_index residue agmata backbone coil disoMine earlyFolding helix ppII sheet sidechain seq_A 0 M 0.0 0.697 0.499 0.947 0.044 0.266 0.105 0.117 0.484 seq_A 1 D 0.001 0.702 0.54 0.966 0.048 0.226 0.118 0.078 0.281 ... seq_A 10 - seq_A 11 - seq_A 12 M 0.002 0.644 0.606 0.989 0.041 0.196 0.126 0.072 0.508
Distribution of predictions along the alignment ............................................... This table is in long (tidy) format: one row per alignment position and predicted feature. The set of columns therefore stays the same whichever predictors are selected, which makes the result directly usable with the *Filter*, *Datamash* and *ggplot2* Galaxy tools. Use *Cut* or a pivot tool if you need one column per feature instead.
- ``median``: median of the values available at that alignment position. - ``first_quartile`` and ``third_quartile``: the 25th and 75th percentiles. - ``bottom_outlier``: first quartile minus 1.5 times the interquartile range. - ``top_outlier``: third quartile plus 1.5 times the interquartile range.
Alignment positions where no sequence has a predicted value (an all-gap column) have empty summary values.
::
alignment_position prediction median first_quartile third_quartile bottom_outlier top_outlier 0 agmata 0.0 0.0 0.001 -0.0 0.001 1 agmata 0.001 0.001 0.001 0.001 0.002 ...
Keep in mind that quartiles computed over a handful of sequences are not robust: the wider the alignment, the more meaningful the distribution.
@HELP_ABOUT@
